payload.answer: [hard] The ledger is append-only: every transition is a recorded event; wind-back NEVER rewrites or deletes history, it records a new position. [hard] A leased job cannot be stopped by mutating the row out from under a live worker -- decide explicitly how stop interacts with an in-flight lease (cooperative via the lease, or stop-after-current), and note the worker now drains on SIGTERM, which is the same class of problem already solved once. [hard] Never block a worker on a human. [hard] Every job stays idempotent under replay. [hard] Domain purity: the state machine belongs in domain/ as pure functions, with the repository and CLI as thin shells over it. [hard] Coordinate with two sibling projects: abandon-command also needs to settle in-flight jobs when a project is abandoned, and fork-command also needs a way to address a past point in a job's history -- do not invent a third addressing scheme. [hard] Conventional Commits, feature branch into develop.

A written state machine covering every legal transition among ready, leased, succeeded, failed, awaiting_human, awaiting_capacity and cancelled, including which are reachable by operator command and which only by the worker. Four commands implemented against it. CANCELLED is written by exactly one path and observable in `vibey status`. Each command is idempotent: stopping a stopped job, continuing a running job, restarting a fresh job all succeed quietly rather than erroring or double-acting. All 7 gates green including 100% branch coverage of the new transitions.

None of the four exist today, and the gap has a smoking gun: CANCELLED is declared in the JobState enum at domain/job.py line 14 and is NEVER WRITTEN by anything in the codebase. `vibey status` prints a 'CANCELLED: 0' line -- a counter for a state that cannot occur. JobRepository exposes enqueue, claim, heartbeat, ack, nack, defer, park, reap, assign_engine, count_unsettled, queue_depth, get: no stop, no rewind, no restart. 'Continue' partially exists but only by accident of other features -- answering a human gate flips awaiting_human back to ready, and `vibey design resume` re-enqueues the interview -- so there is no way to continue a job that failed out its max_attempts. The practical consequence is that a job going wrong can only be watched until it fails.

Four CLI commands over ONE job state machine: stop a job, wind a job back to an earlier point, continue a job, and restart a job from scratch. They are deliberately one piece of work rather than four, because they cannot be designed independently -- stop and restart must agree on what CANCELLED means before either can be written, and wind-back and continue must agree on what a restored point contains. Design the state machine first, then the four verbs fall out of it.

payload.answer: When a job is stuck, mis-aimed, or burning credits on the wrong thing -- the operator watching a session go somewhere useless and having no button. Stop marks it CANCELLED so it will not be retried, and lets the current lease drain rather than yanking it: the worker finishes the turn in hand and claims no more. That is not a new mechanism to invent -- the SIGTERM drain added for Kubernetes scale-in already does exactly this, and stop should reuse the concept rather than grow a second one. The job stays in history; the ledger is append-only and a stopped job is evidence, not an embarrassment to erase.

When a job went off-track partway and the work before that point is still good -- a wrong design direction, a bad review verdict, a deploy that failed for a reason since fixed. Specify the point by ledger seq: the ledger is append-only, project-scoped, totally ordered, and already indexed as event_project_seq, so a seq is stable across worker restarts and machines. Crucially the fork-command project has independently landed on the same answer for the same reason -- do not let the two invent different addressing schemes, or an operator will have to learn both. Wind-back RECORDS a new position; it never rewrites or truncates history. The open design question worth real thought is what 'restoring' means beyond the queue row: the git worktree and the engine's own rundir state are not in the ledger, so be explicit about what is restored and what is merely re-derivable, rather than implying a completeness the mechanism cannot deliver.
